item.title: Structure Biology
item.description:
Structural biology is a powerful approach to understanding the molecular basis of biological processes by revealing the three-dimensional architecture of biomolecules. Our research focuses on elucidating the structural mechanisms underlying key cellular events, with a particular emphasis on protein–lipid interactions, vesicle trafficking, and membrane-associated complexes involved in neuronal function and disease. By integrating cutting-edge techniques such as cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM), cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET), and in-cell NMR spectroscopy, we aim to capture biomolecular structures in their native environments and dynamic states. These structural insights are further complemented by biochemical assays, functional studies, and computational modeling to link molecular architecture to biological function. Ultimately, our goal is to uncover how structural alterations contribute to aging, neurodegeneration, and other disease processes, paving the way for the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.

item.title: 🧑 Aging and Aging-Related Diseases
item.description:
Aging is a fundamental biological process marked by the progressive decline of cellular and physiological functions, leading to increased vulnerability to diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and Parkinson’s disease (PD). Our research aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying aging and neurodegeneration, with a particular focus on how protein–lipid interactions, vesicle dynamics, and membrane biology contribute to neuronal aging and dysfunction. By combining in situ structural biology, mass spectrometry–based lipidomics, and cellular and animal models, we seek to understand how lipid signaling and vesicle trafficking change during aging and how these changes influence disease progression. Furthermore, we aim to identify biomarkers and therapeutic targets by integrating molecular data with disease phenotypes. Ultimately, our goal is to translate these mechanistic insights into novel strategies for early diagnosis, intervention, and treatment of aging-related neurodegenerative disorders, thereby contributing to healthier aging and improved quality of life in the elderly population.

item.title: Lipidomics
item.description:
Lipids are fundamental biomolecules that play critical roles in maintaining cellular structure, energy storage, and signaling. Beyond their structural and metabolic functions, lipids are key regulators of diverse biological processes, including membrane dynamics, vesicle trafficking, inflammation, and cell death. Dysregulation of lipid metabolism is increasingly recognized as a hallmark of numerous diseases, such as neurodegenerative disorders, metabolic syndromes, and cancer. Our research focuses on systematically characterizing the lipid landscape and understanding how lipid composition, distribution, and interactions change under physiological and pathological conditions. We employ state-of-the-art mass spectrometry–based lipidomics, in combination with advanced separation technologies, chemical labeling strategies, and integrative bioinformatics analysis, to achieve comprehensive and quantitative profiling of lipid species. Furthermore, we explore how lipids interact with proteins and other biomolecules to modulate cellular signaling and function. Ultimately, our goal is to link lipid alterations to disease mechanisms, identify novel lipid biomarkers, and uncover therapeutic targets. By advancing the field of lipidomics, our research seeks to provide deeper insights into lipid biology and its implications for human health and disease.
